youtube.title: The Goalkeeper Who Did Nothing and Won #Shorts
youtube.description:
Last kick of the final. Every keeper dives. Leo doesn't.

A study of 286 penalty kicks in top leagues found keepers dived left or right about 94% of the time - yet, given where strikers actually aim, staying in the middle was the best bet. Psychologists call it action bias: a goal after a dive feels like bad luck, a goal while you stood still feels like your fault.

The catch: a later study argues that if every keeper stayed, strikers would simply aim for the middle.

Would you have had the nerve to stand still?

Sources:
- Bar-Eli, Azar, Ritov, Keidar-Levin & Schein (2007), Action bias among elite soccer goalkeepers: The case of penalty kicks, Journal of Economic Psychology 28(5): https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/joepsy/v28y2007i5p606-621.html
- Study record: https://cris.huji.ac.il/en/publications/action-bias-among-elite-soccer-goalkeepers-the-case-of-penalty-ki-2/
- Press coverage (94%): https://www.jpost.com/health-and-sci-tech/science-and-environment/article-124988
- Reanalysis (strategic interaction, 1,043 Bundesliga kicks): https://lida.sport-iat.de/twm/Record/4019956?lng=en

Leo and the match are fictional; the numbers come from the study.
AI disclosure: made with AI assistance (script drafting, synthetic narration voice, animation).
